date.description: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD; use dateEnd for ranges. Bare YYYY is allowed because some records are known only to the year, and inventing a month would assert precision the source does not have.

items.description:
The subject area a record belongs to. A TAG SET, not a partition: a ledger record carries `domains[]` and may carry several, a series carries exactly one, and a phase is not a domain — phase 7 produced eight records filed across seven values.

THE DISTINCTION THAT GETS CONFUSED IS welfare AGAINST human-development: welfare is the DELIVERY of a scheme, human-development is the OUTCOME it was meant to produce. Records carrying both (Swachh Bharat, PM-JAY, the anaemia reversal) are the normal case, not an error — the scheme is one domain and what it did to people is another.
- macro: aggregate economic conditions and fiscal or monetary policy.
- banking: banks, credit, financial supervision and resolution.
- employment: work, labour force, earnings and formality.
- poverty: measured deprivation and consumption-based poverty.
- human-development: outcomes in health, nutrition and survival — what delivery produced.
- infrastructure: physical networks and their capacity or service.
- welfare: scheme delivery and entitlements — what was provided.
- governance: institutions of state, enforcement, transparency and rights.
- kashmir: a cross-cutting lens, applied to records whose primary subject sits elsewhere.
- federalism: Centre-state relations. Also a lens: GST and groundwater carry it alongside their own subject.
- foreign: trade, external balances and relations with other states.
- defence: military and security. One record; sparsely attested.
- environment: land, water, air and the resource base.
- demography: population structure. NEVER USED — no record or series carries it, so its intended boundary is unattested and this line describes the word, not observed practice.

type.description:
What KIND of thing the record is — not what domain it concerns and not how it turned out.
The distinction that gets confused is a measure the state chose against a disruption it did not: see the note on `shock`.
- reform: a measure the state deliberately introduced — a law, scheme, programme or rate change.
- event: a discrete dated occurrence, over in days or weeks.
- episode: a pattern or contested question observed over a span, with no single act at its centre.
- shock: a disruption arriving from outside the government's control.
- institutional: a change to the rules of the game or to a standing body, rather than a programme run through one.
USAGE NOTE, unresolved: `shock` is currently applied both to external disruptions (the taper tantrum, COVID, US tariffs) and to domestically caused failures (the IL&FS collapse; the 2020 migrant exodus, whose own caseAgainst records that the four hours' notice "was a choice"). The definition above states the external reading, which fits three of the five. The other two have not been reclassified.

claimAtLaunch.description: What the government said this would achieve, where applicable

assessment.description:
What the record concludes. These values had no written definitions until 2026-08-01, which is how `reversed` came to cover two different mechanisms without the type objecting. Definitions:
- worked: the measure achieved the objective stated at announcement, on the evidence available.
- partly: the measure achieved part of its stated objective, or achieved it for part of the intended population.
- failed: the measure did not achieve the objective stated at announcement. Includes a measure struck down by a court, because the outcome is the same and only the mechanism differs — record the mechanism in assessmentNote.
- reversed: the ENACTING AUTHORITY withdrew or repealed its own measure. Judicial invalidation is NOT reversed: a court striking a measure down is not the enacting authority changing its mind, and collapsing the two loses the thing that distinguishes a government retreating under pressure from a government overruled.
- contested: the evidence supports more than one defensible reading and the record does not choose between them.
- too-early: the measure is in force but has not run long enough for its stated objective to be testable.
- baseline-context: pre-2014 context, carried so that post-2014 records are read against a stated starting condition. Never scored; the schema ties it to term "baseline".

shockExposure.description: Which external shocks confound assessment of this record, if any

tier.description:
Evidence grade of the DOCUMENT ACTUALLY RETRIEVED, not of the institution the subject belongs to. This is the operative rule and the one that goes wrong: a CAG finding known only through a newspaper's account of an RTI reply is T4, because the subject is official but the evidence is relayed. Grade what you hold, not what it is about.
- T1: official Indian statistical or institutional source, retrieved directly - a ministry release, an RBI, MoSPI or NCRB publication, a CAG report, a Parliamentary reply.
- T2: multilateral or international statistical source, retrieved directly - World Bank, IMF, ILO, WHO.
- T3: peer-reviewed research or a working paper.
- T4: reported or documentary journalism, NGO datasets, and anything RELAYED rather than retrieved - including an official figure known only through a press account, and an RTI reply cited but not obtained.
- T5: contested composite index. Always carries a dispute record covering its own domain (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
Note that tier is asserted in exactly one place per layer: on the series itself, or on each entry of a ledger or provenance `sources[]`. A series `source` is a SourceRef and carries NO tier - the object is closed, so a tier inside it is rejected rather than silently ignored.

confidence.description:
How firmly the record's FINDING is established. Distinct from `tier`, which grades the evidence retrieved: a record can rest on a single relayed source and still be high-confidence if what it asserts is not in doubt, and can rest on a primary source and be medium if the reading is contested.
- high: the finding is well established and would survive a hostile reading.
- medium: the finding holds but rests on incomplete retrieval or a contested reading.
- low: the finding is provisional and should not be leaned on.
USAGE NOTE, unresolved: the field is ambiguous in practice between confidence in the FINDING and how well RETRIEVED the record is. L-0014 is high on a single T4 source while L-0015 is medium on a T1, which fits the finding reading; L-0089's revisitTrigger ties confidence to retrieving two primary documents, which fits the retrieval reading. The distribution is also heavily skewed — 63 high, 24 medium, 2 low across 89 records — so `low` is close to unattested. Nothing has been reclassified.

asOf.description: Date this record was last researched/updated

caveat.description: A blocking qualification that MUST render wherever this record appears, including compact listings. Use only when the record would mislead without it — an unverified comparability assumption, a circular measure, a disputed instrument. Not for ordinary uncertainty, which belongs in notes. Authored forms range from a short headline flag ("T5 CONTESTED INDEX") to a full sentence; the floor exists to stop an empty stub, not to require prose.

unmeasured.description: Dimensions this record SHOULD have but which have no measurement. An absence is a research finding, not an empty cell — declaring it here keeps it visible in every view rather than only where a component happens to supply it. Use when a chain has a missing link, an intended outcome was never measured, or a series stops short of the thing it is cited to demonstrate.

what.description: The thing that is not measured, stated positively

why.description: Why no figure exists — not collected, not published, withheld, or never defined

wouldFill.description: The source that would close it, if one is identifiable. Doubles as a verification-queue seed.

reasonKind.description:
The STATED reason no figure exists — what the responsible body says, not what is true. Where the stated reason is contradicted, set reasonDisputed and carry the contradiction in `why`.

THE TEST IS WHETHER THE DATA EXISTS, asked in this order:
- not-collected: never gathered. No record exists to release. If the holder were compelled tomorrow they would have nothing to produce.
- not-published: exists in a holder's hands, not released. The test is producibility under compulsion, not whether anyone has asked.
- withheld: exists, release was specifically requested or legally required, and was refused. Narrower than not-published — requires an identifiable refusal, not merely absence of release.
- never-defined: no agreed definition exists for the quantity, so it could not be collected even in principle. NOT "nobody has studied it" — an unstudied but definable quantity is not-collected.

reasonDisputed.description: True where the stated reason is contradicted by evidence — for example a body saying data was never maintained while another arm of the same government publishes some of it. The contradiction must be stated in `why`. This is not a fifth reasonKind: it is a dispute about which kind applies.

disputeKind.description:
What kind of contradiction reasonDisputed records. Required when reasonDisputed is true.
- evidentiary: the stated reason is contradicted by evidence that the data exists or was held.
- normative: the factual claim is not contested; what is contested is the characterisation of the non-release, typically against a legal or judicial obligation.

differentFacts.description: True where the two sides of the record do not share a common measure. Three conditions, of which the third is operative: (a) PRECONDITION — caseFor and caseAgainst cite different underlying quantities, measures or events, not the same one weighted differently. (b) PRECONDITION — neither case contradicts the other's factual claim, so granting one side's strongest fact in full leaves the other's case intact. (c) OPERATIVE — no single measure exists, or could be constructed from available data, that places both sides' facts on one ledger. An UNBUILT comparison FAILS (c): if a common denominator exists in principle and merely has not been built, that is a gap in the instrument, not a property of the argument. A counterpart that is DECLARED UNMEASURABLE passes (c). In practice (c) admits only arguments that cross a category boundary — a quantity against a legal ruling, a constitutional process, or a stated absence. Two economic cases almost always share a ledger in principle: an incidence analysis, a disposition table, a water-productivity account. The worked negative is the implicit taxation of farmers, where the OECD Producer Support Estimate nets budgetary support against implicit price transfers by construction.

differentFactsNote.description: What each side is counting, and why both can be arithmetically correct. Required in practice wherever differentFacts is true.

assessmentNote.description: A note on the assessment VALUE itself — typically that the existing vocabulary does not cleanly fit and the value may change on review. Not a note on the finding, which belongs in caseFor/caseAgainst.

revisitTrigger.description: A stated condition under which this record should be re-tested. Used where a judgement is correct now but rests on something that will change — most often a common measure that cannot yet be built but will become buildable. Distinct from assessmentNote, which is about the assessment VALUE rather than about when to look again.
